doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Raeburn's band after Mandel left
summary: After Mandel left, Raeburn reorganized in Los Angeles with Si Zentner, Johnny Richards and Handy's Dalvatore Sally, and the band folded in 1946.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Um-hm, when you were in the band was Harry Klee, there already?

No he came later. He came after I, after I’d left the band by then, gone with Jimmy Dorsey, that was when Boyd came into Los Angeles organized a whole different band. I think Si Zentner [Simon Hugh “Si” Zentner] took my place, he opened at a place called the, a place on Hollywood Boulevard, El Morocco or some kind of name like that and he had six woodwinds something I’d love to have had. He had Klee and some guy, Ralph Lee, a good player, who played all the doubles.

And Johnny Richards was the arranger and by then they were trying to do more of a Kenton type thing. And that was when George had written, “Dalvatore Sally,” and all those other things, those were written after I’d left the band.

Yeah ‘46, yeah that’s right, cause the band broke up shortly after that. Boyd never really had a big working band again except for pick up dates and that isn’t the kind of music you could play on pick up dates.
No. It was complicated music, but it was fun to play.
